what: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: goal CleanLASA make easy import clean LASA (Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam) SPSS data files R. applies correct variable value labels LASA documentation, handles differences waves, flags variables matched documentation can checked manually, helps find open right LASA documentation topic file code. Variable value-label metadata hand-transcribed per file code. ’s parsed programmatically LASA’s variable-information PDFs single normalized database (lasa_label_db()), bundled package refreshable time update_lasa_labels().

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: can install development version CleanLASA GitHub :
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("Highmeadows/CleanLASA")

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: main entry point read_lasa_sav(), detects LASA datafile ’re working (file name) labels using package’s label database automatically:
code: library(CleanLASA)  # Import and label a LASA .sav file  # importing the data should generally be in this format: data <- read_lasa_sav("path/to/LASA[wave][file_code].sav")  # Specific examples: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav") # LASA wave B file 046 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASA_data/LASAZ004.sav") # LASA wave Z file 004 data <- read_lasa_sav("Documents/Research/data/LAS2B011.sav") # LASA wave 2B file 011 data <- read_lasa_sav("lasazoa1.sav") # LASA wave Z file oa1

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: read_lasa_sav() (apply_lasa_labels(), ) accepts five reshaping arguments: name_corrections – manually point canonical suffix (e.g. lphya08) differently-named source column, known typo/renaming data. to_factor – convert categorical variables factors, using SPSS value labels levels. to_numeric – restore count/continuous variables plain numeric, converting negative (missing-reason) codes NA. standardize_names – rename every matched column canonical lowercase LASA name wave code removed (e.g. lphya01), standardize "respnr" (capitalization) "respnr". Always implies split_wavecode = TRUE well. split_wavecode – move wave-letter prefix variable names (e.g. blphya01 becomes lphya01) new "LASA_wave" column, inserted right "respnr" filled file’s wave code (e.g. "B", "2B", "3B"). Regardless arguments, every matched column also keeps original SPSS value coding available reference attributes – attr(x, "original_labels") (codebook) attr(x, "original_values") (raw imported values) – R output can always cross-checked another program’s (e.g. SPSS) coding, even to_numeric/ to_factor reshaping. importing, can check whether variables matched LASA documentation using lasa_label_report(): returns set “faulty” variables — ones couldn’t matched corresponding documentation — can inspect resolve analysis.
code: # Rename columns to their canonical names and split the wave code into its # own column, all in one call: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", standardize_names = TRUE) names(data)[1:3] #> [1] "respnr"    "LASA_wave" "lphya01"  # split_wavecode also works on its own, without fully standardizing names: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", split_wavecode = TRUE) lasa_label_report(data)

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: apply_lasa_labels() applies labelling engine data frame, output read_lasa_sav(). useful transformation (e.g. dplyr::mutate()) stripped attributes, file imported way:
code: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav") data <- dplyr::mutate(data, respnr = respnr) # attributes stripped data <- apply_lasa_labels(data) # re-labels via stored provenance  # Or supply identity explicitly: raw <- haven::read_sav("LASAC046.sav", user_na = TRUE) data <- apply_lasa_labels(raw, filecode = "046", wave = "C")

code: db <- lasa_label_db() subset(db$variables, filecode == "046" & wave == "B")

what: Refreshing coverage from LASA’s own documentation
title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: update_lasa_labels() downloads (reads local copy ) LASA variable-information PDF, parses , merges result local copy database – replacing records PDF documents, never anything unrelated file code:
code: update_lasa_labels(filecode = "046")             # resolve + download + parse update_lasa_labels(url = "https://.../LASA162_varinfo.pdf") update_lasa_labels(filecode = "046", path = "LASA046_varinfo.pdf") # offline

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: PDF missing, unreachable, wrong incomplete variable, manual_update_lasa_labels() patches database directly, without touching requiring PDF. later update_lasa_labels() refresh file code silently discard correction.
code: manual_update_lasa_labels(   filecode = "046", wave = "B", variable = "lphya01",   val_labels = c(`-5` = "NA, wrong, skip")  # merged into the existing set )  manual_update_lasa_labels(   filecode = "046", wave = "all", variable = "lphya01",   val_labels = c(`-5` = "NA, wrong, skip"),   replace_val_labels = TRUE  # replaces the value-label set entirely )

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: lasa_topics() searches LASA topic overview topics, themes, file codes: table built live LASA website first time ’s needed, cached — rest session disk — doesn’t rebuilt every session. Use refresh = TRUE check live site anything new, newly added wave file code. ’ve found topic file code, lasa_var_info() opens variable-information PDF directly LASA website (PDFs bundled package):
code: # Browse everything lasa_topics()  # Search by topic name (fuzzy matching handles typos and partial names) lasa_topics(topic = "physical act")  # Search by theme or subtheme lasa_topics(theme = "cognitive") lasa_topics(theme = "memory") lasa_var_info("046")               # by file code lasa_var_info("LASA046")           # file code variations are recognized lasa_var_info("Physical activity") # or by topic name lasa_var_info("physical act")      # fuzzy matching handles typos too  # Get the URL without opening it url <- lasa_var_info("046", open = FALSE)

title: Apply LASA variable/value labels from the label database — apply_lasa_labels
text: Identity (file code wave) resolved priority order: (1) filecode/wave arguments, supplied; (2) data's "LASA_file_code"/"LASA_wave" attributes; (3) single-valued "LASA_wave" column data (wave – filecode must still come elsewhere); (4) best-effort guess data's object name, happens follow LASA file-naming convention (e.g. data frame literally named LASAB046) – never required, something rely . Column matching tries, order: (1) explicit name_corrections override, (2) exact (case-sensitive) match wave-specific documented name, (3) case-insensitive match name, (4) exact match canonical (wave-stripped) name, (5) case-insensitive match canonical name.

title: Search the LASA topic table — lasa_topics
text: Topic, theme, subtheme matching case-insensitive. Incomplete names small typographical errors accepted fuzzy_match = TRUE. Supplying theme searches main LASA themes subthemes. LASA topics documented several related file codes one row topic table, main file, telephone-interview version, longitudinally cleaned version. LASA site's label row spells (example "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy - tel. respondent"), file code returned part label describes (e.g. "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy" proxy-interview file code) rather full combined label repeated every code. Splitting prefers row's column layout falls back LASA file-code numbering convention (0/1 = main face--face file, 2/3 = processed derived file, 4/5 = longitudinally cleaned revised file, 6 = telephone interview proxy, 7 = telephone interview respondent); single file code covers several qualifiers (nothing disambiguate), full descriptive list dropped favor plain base topic name. small number rows need information present compact topic-table text - lives file code's variable-information PDF, topic page's prose, specific domain knowledge - scraper can derive table alone. rows carry curated, documented correction (see data-raw/lasa_topic_overrides.R package source full list reasoning behind one). curation applied every time table built, independently refresh.

title: Manually correct or add LASA variable/value labels — manual_update_lasa_labels
text: filecode Optional LASA file code (e.g. "046", "zoa1", "z004"). Required variable/wave match one file code, defining brand-new variable existing row matches. wave Optional LASA wave code (e.g. "B", "2B"), "" apply override every wave matched filecode+canonical-name combination exists . Required variable canonical name (carries wave information ), wave-specific name's leading prefix shared one wave (e.g. "b" shared B/2B/3B/MB) thus inferred. variable Required. Either wave-specific variable name (e.g. "blphya01") canonical name (e.g. "lphya01"). var_label Optional replacement variable label. NA/omitted leaves existing label untouched. val_labels Optional named vector value-label corrections, keyed numeric code, e.g. c(\-5\verb = "NA, wrong, skip", \1\verb = "man") (quote backtick negative/numeric-looking names). replace_val_labels Logical, default FALSE. FALSE, val_labels merged existing value-label set (upserted code). TRUE, result val_labels – every coded value variable dropped labels applied.

title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
text: file name parsed LASA naming convention: regular single-letter waves: LASA[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LASAE046.SAV; waves 2B, 3B, 4B, MB: LAS[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LAS3B046.SAV; information stored across waves: wave code Z, e.g. LASAZ004.SAV; file codes contain 2 3 alphanumeric characters interpreted case-insensitively. Column matching, value/variable-label attachment, to_factor/to_numeric reshaping, standardize_names/split_wavecode renaming performed apply_lasa_labels()'s underlying engine, looking metadata parsed file code/wave lasa_label_db(). file code database coverage yet labelled -op (every column left untouched, "found" recorded matching audit) rather error – refresh coverage update_lasa_labels() manual_update_lasa_labels(). labelling, provenance attributes attached: "LASA_wave", "LASA_file_code", "LASA_source_file". lets apply_lasa_labels() re-label object later (e.g. dplyr::mutate() strips attributes) without needing filecode/wave supplied . variable-name matching audit attached generic "label_report" attribute; retrieve lasa_label_report().

text: filecode Optional LASA file code resolve PDF (e.g. "046", "z004", "zoa1", bare group prefix "zoa" unambiguous). Ignored url path supplied. url Optional explicit PDF URL, bypassing file-code resolution. path Optional path already-downloaded PDF, bypassing resolution download – supported way update database without network access. dry_run Logical, default FALSE. TRUE, parse validate usual return structured result, never write database. strict Logical, default TRUE.
